appraisal_events.evidence: « l’horreur de ces amours que l’inquiétude seule a enfantées vient de ce que nous tournons et retournons sans cesse dans notre cage des propos insignifiants » ; « le hasard d’une minute d’angoisse, minute indéfiniment prolongée par notre faiblesse de caractère, laquelle refait chaque soir les expériences et s’abaisse à des calmants » ; « le triste remède de chercher à agir malgré elle […] à ruser nous-même, à nous faire détester ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator turns his own analytic authority against himself, diagnosing his love for Albertine as a caged, anxiety-bred servitude sustained by weakness of will, ruse, and self-degradation. The lucidity of the diagnosis is the narrator's own and is fully endorsed by the text, so the local movement is a clear self-diminishment rather than a neutral report.

appraisal_events.evidence: « celle qui nous résiste et qui nous ment » ; « cette terrible intonation dédaigneuse : “Je lui ai dit non, catégoriquement”, qui se retrouve dans toutes les classes de la société quand une femme ment » ; but also « nous nous étonnons si seulement nous éprouvons, à une brusque résistance, que nous ne disposons pas d’elle » and « l’aveuglement de notre crédulité ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The beloved woman — generalized from Albertine, who is named as the object of this love — is charged with duplicity, mendacity and disdain, yet the passage stages that charge inside a jealousy it has just declared blind and self-manufacturing, so the blame partly discredits its own source. The same movement leaves Albertine holding the leverage: she resists, withholds, and cannot be disposed of.

status_effects.explanation: He is locally reduced to dependence on the person who makes him suffer, with any relief explicitly declared illusory and temporary (« l’inquiétude sera tout de même la plus forte »); the brief evocation of complete repose is hypothetical and immediately cancelled, so it does not offset the dominant movement.
He presents himself as weak-willed, scheming, credulous and pettily obsessed with reconstructing insignificant remarks — a self-portrait that lowers him even as the analysis is sharp.
Her resistance and reticence give her the upper hand: the narrator discovers he does not dispose of her, must thank her for her confidences and dare not answer back.
She is characterized as duplicitous and lying, but the charge is weakened by the passage's own exposure of the jealous lover's blindness, so the diminishment is real yet not securely endorsed.

ambiguities: The last two paragraphs shift from « Albertine » to a generic « elle » / « la femme que nous aimons »; the accusation of lying is voiced as a universal maxim, and reading Albertine as its target depends on the essay's explicit anchoring in « mon amour pour Albertine ».
